claims: Law graduates covered by the Legal Services Award get 150% for the first 3 hours of overtime and 200% after that.
whys: The penalties table and overtime list (lines 98-106) attach the 150%/200% split only to Monday to Saturday until 12 noon. Overtime after 12 noon Saturday and on Sunday is 200% from the first hour, and public holidays are 250%. The FAQ answer leaves out that condition, so it overstates the 150% band for weekend overtime. This pass cannot add the time condition because it would add new figures.
constants: Legal Services Award cl 20.2 (penalties/overtime arrays in lawyer.ts)
reviewerNotes: I agree with the writer's factQuestion. The FAQ attaches the 150%/200% split to all law graduate overtime, but cl 20.2 (the penalties array, lines 98-106) limits it to Monday to Saturday until 12 noon. Overtime from Saturday 12 noon and on Sunday is 200% from the first hour. This pass cannot add the condition.

claims: FAQ 'Does a Certificate III in pathology collection increase your pay?' answers 'Yes, once you have 12 months' experience.'
'Does a Certificate III in pathology collection increase your pay?' answers 'Yes, once you have 12 months' experience.'
whys: The page's own table pays more for a Cert III before 12 months too. A qualified collector under 12 months is Level 6 at $30.63, and an unqualified one under 12 months is Level 5 at $30.45. So the 'once you have 12 months' condition looks wrong. The bigger gap ($32.67 vs $31.67/$30.63) only opens after 12 months.

The page's own table pays a Cert III collector more before 12 months too: Level 6 at $30.63 against Level 5 at $30.45. From 12 months to 2 years the gap is larger: Level 7 qualified at $32.67 against Level 6 unqualified at $30.63. The condition 'once you have 12 months' understates when the Cert III premium starts.
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's question. The FAQ says a Cert III raises pay 'once you have 12 months' experience', but by the page's own table a Cert III already pays more under 12 months (Level 6 at $30.63 vs Level 5 at $30.45). Between 12 months and 2 years the gap is $32.67 vs $30.63. Passed on as a fact question, text not changed.
